feature.hypothesis: on_pair already holds every class-matched candidate and select_detection returns only the one pallet stage 2 estimates, so the controller's pose names neither the sent index nor the deferred indices of this capture. select_stage2_subset returns both vectors with that same ranking, and writing those indices onto PalletPoseStamped, and onto the failure diagnostic when no pose is published, is the sent-versus-deferred split for this synchronized capture.
feature.summary: For the class-matched detections in one capture, select_stage2_subset ranks that DetectionCandidate list with the strategy select_detection already implements. It applies that strategy by the first-maximum rule std::max_element already uses, so a tie keeps the earlier candidate and the later tied candidate stays deferred. It admits at most the count the caller passes, in that rank order, and places every candidate it does not admit into deferred, preserving their order in the candidate list. Each candidate keeps its source_index. Stage2Admission holds those two vectors, admitted and deferred. An empty candidate list returns both vectors empty, and an unknown strategy throws. The pose node calls it with its detection_selection strategy and a count of one, so stage 2 still estimates that single admitted pallet. The admitted source index and the deferred source indices are written on PalletPoseStamped after input_depth_stamp. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the split is this capture while the scene can still change. When the estimate fails, publish no PalletPoseStamped and write the same two lists on the failure diagnostic, which is the only result that path publishes. The two early returns that publish nothing stay as they are. The user named which detections are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred. The part they did not name is that the split is these two admission vectors, ordered by that first-maximum rule, on the pose result the handling process reads.

method:
Adopt this method. For the class-matched detections in one capture, select_stage2_subset ranks that DetectionCandidate list with the same strict-weak comparator select_detection already uses. highest_confidence orders by score, then area_px. largest_area orders by area_px, then score. source_index is not a key. A comparator that uses <= is not a strict weak ordering. std::max_element returns the first greatest element and replaces its champion only when that champion is strictly less than the next candidate, so a tie keeps the earlier candidate and the later tied candidate stays deferred. A tie is both keys equal. Under highest_confidence a later box with the same score and a larger area_px is strictly greater. Under largest_area the keys are reversed. NumPy argmax and Python max return that same first maximum. An empty candidate list returns both vectors empty before the strategy check and before max_element, because an empty range returns last and must not be dereferenced. Any other strategy string throws std::invalid_argument and is not turned into a diagnostic.

Admission repeats that first maximum on the candidates not yet chosen, up to the count the caller passes, and stops at that count. admitted holds those winners in that rank order. One forward pass over the original vector appends every unchosen candidate to deferred, in candidate-list order. Each copied candidate keeps its source_index, the slot in this Detection2DArray, not Detection2D.id. Stage2Admission holds those two vectors. std::stable_sort preserves the relative order of equivalent elements, so its prefix can match that admitted order, but the tail of the sort is rank order and is not the deferred vector. std::partial_sort does not preserve the order of equivalent elements and leaves the unselected range in an unspecified order. std::stable_partition would keep the admitted side in input order, which is not rank order. A count of one admits the same candidate select_detection returns. A larger count than the list admits every candidate and leaves deferred empty.

The pose node calls select_stage2_subset with its detection_selection strategy and a count of one, so stage 2 estimates that single admitted pallet and does not estimate deferred candidates. On success, PalletPoseStamped gains an int32 admitted_source_index and an int32[] deferred_source_indices after input_depth_stamp. Fields already on the message stay in place and stay filled. The pose header stamp stays the publish time. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps. ApproximateTime can match stamps that differ inside the configured interval, so the two lists are this pair only. An admitted index of 0 is a real detections slot. An empty deferred sequence means this pair had one class-matched candidate. geometry_msgs/PoseStamped stays a header and a pose.

When the estimate fails, publish no PalletPoseStamped. The only result is the existing WARN DiagnosticStatus. Write the same two lists as two KeyValue entries on that status: admitted_source_index as decimal text, and deferred_source_indices as one comma-separated string in deferred order. One key holds one string, so a repeated key hides the list. Keep the status name, hardware id, WARN level, failure message, failure_reason, and both capture stamps. An empty deferred list is an empty string. The two early returns that publish nothing stay as they are: the empty-candidate return, and the depth-conversion return. An unknown detection_selection still throws rather than becoming a diagnostic.

Soft-NMS decays overlapping scores and can make a later box the next maximum; it does not leave every unselected candidate in input order. OpenCV NMS stable-sorts score and index so an equal score keeps the earlier index, then returns only the surviving indices. Weighted Boxes Fusion replaces a cluster with one confidence-weighted rectangle. DETR assigns a fixed query set with the Hungarian algorithm and drops non-maximum suppression. ByteTrack puts high-score boxes in one set and low-score boxes in another, associates the high set first, and deletes tracks that stay unmatched. ifm getPallet returns up to 10 pallets reordered by palletOrder, default scoreDescending, and palletIndex is a template type from 0 to 9. Isaac ROS FoundationPose builds the stage-2 mask from the highest-scoring detection. Detection2DArrayFilter replaces its running detection only when the score is strictly greater, so a tie keeps the earlier detection, and it publishes that one Detection2D without the detections it did not select. Lang2Lift selects the mask with the highest quality score and calls FoundationPose once. Wu and Demeester write a 6D pose for each detected pallet bin. Detection3D, PalletDetection, and PoseStamped have no deferred-index field. Detection2D.id may be empty and is an id across messages, not the slot in this array.

The rank is that linear first-maximum pass plus the walk that copies deferred. The cost that scales is one stage-2 estimate per admitted candidate. Classic chamfer measured 17.59 microseconds per hypothesis, oriented chamfer 51.50 microseconds, and directional chamfer 0.40 microseconds. CosyPose spent 190 ms of a 320 ms scene posing every candidate. Faster R-CNN region-wise time, including NMS, pooling, fully connected layers, and softmax, was 174 ms at about 2000 proposals and 47 ms at 300. A count of one stays at the single estimate, and each deferred source index is not another hypothesis. One int32 and a short int32[] sit in the payload range where ROS 2 end-to-end latency was equal from 128 bytes through 10 KB. REP-107's diagnostic channel is not a keepalive, and aggregation can leave it stale, so the success-path lists are on PalletPoseStamped. The failure path carries the same two lists on the one diagnostic that path publishes.

The bilinear reads are Eigen column-major points(i, 0) and points(i, 1), a stride of N doubles. At 45700 evaluations the translation copy is 133078400 bytes and the sort copy is 66539200 bytes, before the sort itself.

Before the grid, and only for the candidate select_detection already chose: depth_image_to_meters convertTo-copies the whole depth frame into a new CV_32FC1 once per synced pair (camera.yaml depth is 640x480; 16UC1 is scaled by depth_scale 0.001), so that copy does not multiply with deferred indexes. build_bbox_mask zero-fills a 1920x1080 mask and erodes it erode_px 2 times with a 3x3 kernel, even though only the bbox rectangle is set. sample_face_points scans every depth pixel, O(Hd*Wd) = 307200, with a K_inv ray, an SE(3) into RGB, and a lookup in that full mask; the bbox does not cull the depth loop. Accepted points go into per-thread std::vector<Eigen::Vector3d> buckets that together reserve Hd*Wd/4 (76800 Vector3d, about 1.8 MB) and are copied again, row by row, into points_depth_frame. ransac_plane_fit (up to ransac_iters 100, early stop at inlier ratio 0.85) allocates a residual array and a bool mask of length n_face_points every iteration, then copies inliers into a fresh matrix for JacobiSVD. plane_inlier_mask allocates those arrays again, and the pipeline copies the inliers a second time into plane_points_3d. project_points_to_plane_2d allocates an n_plane_inliers x 3 relative matrix and an n_plane_inliers x 2 result; PCA centres another n_plane_inliers x 2 copy. The distance image is built once per detection, not per pose. rasterize_points_to_mask uses resolution_m 0.005 and padding_m 0.80: a nominal 1.20 m by 0.14 m face is 561 by 350 (padded x span 2.8 m; padded y span 1.7400000000000002 m so ceil(span/0.005) is 349 and the +1 makes 350). close_mask clones the mask, runs a 5x5 elliptical MORPH_CLOSE (close_radius_px 2), then connectedComponentsWithStats and a second full-size mask. extract_boundary_mask erodes with a 3x3 kernel and builds another edge image. compute_distance_transform_v2 calls cv::distanceTransform with DIST_L2 and DIST_MASK_PRECISE and convertTo to CV_32FC1. The prototype cache does not reuse that distance image. These passes are smaller than the 45692-evaluation grid and would repeat for each extra posed detection.

Stage 1 is a separate process and is not where the admitted and deferred source indexes are published. rtdetr_detector_node defaults to backend mock, which skips inference copies. detector.yaml and full_pipeline.launch.py set backend tensorrt at input 640 with max_detections 10 and no NMS. On that path image_to_rgb copies msg.data via bytes() into a 1920x1080x3 array (about 6.2 MB; bgr8 reverses channels into a second array), preprocess resizes to 640x640 and builds a float32 CHW ascontiguousarray (1x3x640x640, about 4.9 MB), and TensorRTBackend.infer copies into pinned host memory, memcpy HtoD, execute_async_v3, memcpy DtoH, then copies labels, boxes, and scores back. That host traffic is upstream of the pair delivered to on_pair. The admission integers do not change it. geometry_core links Eigen3, OpenCV core/imgproc, yaml-cpp, and OpenMP; yaml-cpp loads the camera model only in the pose-node constructor, not per frame.
